findings.issue: The non-inferiority pass rule (LB > -0.06) has no assay-sensitivity condition, so H-E1 can be declared SUPPORTED when neither mass ranks affected channels. Detection is close to automatic for long events: 30 of the 91 test events last at least 24 h and 17 last at least 7 days, so under a label-independent Bernoulli flag model at the 1 percent nominal flag rate implied by the 0.99 threshold about 59 of 91 events are detected by chance (40 with probability above 0.95; about 51 at 0.5 percent). Their peak windows are maxima over thousands of near-nominal windows. If native and feature AUROC both sit near 0.5 with small variance, D is near 0, LB exceeds -0.06, and four of five detectors pass while the arm has learned nothing about channel evidence.
findings.evidence: ESA_ADB_PROTOCOL_CANDIDATE_V2.json fields hypothesis_H_E1.per_detector_test and decision_rule; f3_schema/event_schema_table.csv test-event durations recounted in the reviewer's scratch script (median 6.1 h, 75th percentile 77.7 h); models.threshold (0.99 quantile of nominal validation).
findings.required_change: Amend per_detector_test to: 'A detector is evaluable iff n >= 30 detected scoreable events with 0 < m < C AND its native mass passes assay sensitivity: the one-sided 95 percent lower bound of the native mean AUROC (5th percentile of 2,000 event-resampled means, numpy default_rng(20260926 + 100 + model_index)) exceeds 0.5. A detector that fails assay sensitivity is reported NOT_INFORMATIVE and does not count toward k. Among evaluable detectors, pass iff LB > -delta.' Persist the assay statistic, its bound and the pass flag in the decision artifact.

findings.issue: The public freeze is required only 'before the evaluation stage opens test labels', and the change prohibition is keyed to 'after test labels are opened'. The fit:<set>:<model>:<rep> units write validation AND test scores, and the episodes units write thresholds, flags and episode counts, all before that point. Flag rates, episode counts and threshold values are outcome-informative without any label (for example a 40 percent flag rate for a detector), so the threshold rule, mass definitions, margin or decision rule could be changed after seeing them while honoring the letter of the lock. The protocol nowhere forbids inspecting test-period scores before the freeze.

findings.required_change: Set public_freeze.when to: 'After the independent review and the editor's decision, before any fit:<set>:<model>:<rep> unit on the full data and before any test-period window is scored. Only prep:<channel>, stdz:<set> and the PT1-PT3 smoke on the bounded 2006-07-01..2007-06-30 subset may precede the freeze; the smoke's scores, thresholds, flag rates and episode counts are quarantined (hash-recorded in the freeze package, not inspected).' Change stop rule 6 to 'after the public freeze, no change to mission, channel set, split, windows, thresholds, masses, metrics, margin or rule' and add 'no test-period score, flag, threshold, episode count or flag rate is inspected before the freeze'.

findings.issue: Zero-order-hold resampling turns every unlabeled data gap into windows of constant values (sd, slope and delta exactly zero in many channels at once), and these windows are 'valid' under the finiteness rule. Gaps are frequent and long: the 30 s channels have 0.2-0.5 percent of intervals above 30 s with maxima near 5.9 h, channels 64-66 reach 28 h, channels 70-76 reach 13 days and channels 61-63 reach 23 days (channel_sampling.csv). All four labeled communication gaps lie in the fit period, so every test-period gap is unlabeled and any episode it triggers is a false alarm attributed to whichever channel's frozen features are most unusual. The VOR (Appendix B.2) records that sampling-rate gaps are detected as anomalies by many algorithms. E2's concentration and dominant-channel statistics and E3's spike correlations could therefore be preprocessing artifacts of the arm itself, and the protocol has no staleness diagnostic and no sensitivity.
findings.evidence: f3_schema/channel_sampling.csv columns max_interval_s and share_intervals_gt_30s; F3_FACTS.json events_by_split_and_category (fit|Communication Gap 4, none in test); esa_adb_dmlr2026.txt Appendix B.2 and C.3; protocol preprocessing_label_free.windows ('valid iff every analysed channel is finite').
findings.required_change: Add a label-free per-window staleness feature computed in prep:<channel>: age_c = window end time minus the timestamp of the last original sample at or before the window end; window staleness = max over analysed channels of age_c; store it beside the features and cover it in PT2. Fix before freeze: a window is 'stale' iff staleness > 3,600 s (four times the slowest 900 s cadence). Prespecify: (i) report the share of stale windows per period and, per detector, the share of flagged windows, episodes, false-alarm episodes and detected-event peak windows that are stale; (ii) recompute E2, E3 and E4 excluding episodes whose peak window is stale as a prespecified sensitivity; (iii) leave the primary definitions and H-E1 unchanged.

findings.issue: S_L promises E1 on the six-channel lightweight refit with chance levels for C = 6, but this analysis cannot be executed as written: of the 65 test events touching channels 41-46, 62 affect all six channels (m = C, AUROC undefined, Hit@k trivially 1) and only 3 have 0 < m < 6 (id_157 m = 5, id_42 m = 1, id_55 m = 3). findings.issue: The test period is seven years scored against a threshold calibrated on three months of 2006, and the VOR (Table 6, Mission1) documents severe concept drift in channel groups 4, 7 and 13 during the last 18 months, i.e. from about 2012-07-01. 21 of the 91 test events start in that window, and 21 of the 23 three-channel test anomalies affect channels 14, 21 and 29, which are group 4, a drift group. A fixed threshold can flag the drift era almost continuously, producing giant true-alarm episodes (the V5 failure pattern) and shifting the false-alarm set to the pre-drift years. Because exploratory authorization is 'none', a period split cannot be added after results exist.
findings.evidence: esa_adb_dmlr2026.txt Table 6 (Mission1 'Last 18 months include a severe concept drift in channels from groups 4, 7, and 13'); meta_channels.csv groups; event_schema_table.csv start times (2012: 10 events, 2013: 14 events); recount of the three-channel events' channel sets; protocol post_gate_continuation.exploratory_non_rescue.authorization = none.

findings.issue: Detection context omits the two references a reviewer will ask for. First, raw event recall is not interpretable when most long events are detected by chance (see F1-01), and no chance-detection reference is planned. Second, the VOR's primary metric (corrected event-wise precision, recall and F0.5, Eq. 1-2) is what readers will compare against: its Table 4 reports event-wise precision below 0.001 for every unsupervised detector on the full Mission1 channel set, so the arm's detectors must be placed on that scale to show what queue the masses are being evaluated on.

findings.issue: The declared deviation rationale 'svd_solver=full is the solver the synthetic core resolved to by default' is false. In scikit-learn 1.5 and later, including the 1.7.2 runtime of the fresh replication and the planned 1.9.0, svd_solver='auto' resolves to 'covariance_eigh' whenever n_features <= 1000 and n_samples >= 10 x n_features, which holds for the synthetic core (2,277 x 48) and for the ESA fit (100,000 x 232); in scikit-learn before 1.5 the same shapes resolved to 'randomized'. The numerical consequence is small for 10 components, but a frozen protocol must not carry a false fidelity statement.
findings.evidence: Installed scikit-learn 1.9.0, sklearn/decomposition/_pca.py PCA._fit 'auto' branch read locally by the reviewer; manuscript Appendix app:custody (scikit-learn 1.7.2); github-telemetry_alarm_xai/code/models.py line 67 (PCA(n_components=10, random_state=rep_seed)).
findings.required_change: Replace the rationale. In both cases state that 'full', 'covariance_eigh' and the legacy 'randomized' default differ only numerically for 10 components and that random_state is inert for the exact solvers.

findings.issue: The lock says 'Test-period labels are first read by the evaluation stage', but F3 already read every test-period label row (category counts, affected-set sizes, per-event start and end in event_schema_table.csv), and that information changed the primary metric from Hit@3 to AUROC, introduced the m = C exclusion and sized S_L. This is label-structure use, not outcome use, and it is acceptable, but a prospectively frozen protocol must say exactly what was read and what it changed.

findings.issue: E2 entropy and dominant-channel shares are computed on episode-peak masses, whereas tab:mechanism and the matched-information policy inputs used tau-weighted aggregates over all flagged windows of an episode (prepare_inputs.py lines 72-77; run_criticality_unit._aggregate_episode_attributions). Peak-window masses are sharper than aggregates, so E2 concentration values are not comparable with the manuscript's 0.096-0.947 entropies, yet Q-E2 is framed as testing sec:mechanism. The declared deviation is justified only for occlusion and TreeSHAP cost; raw and feature masses over all flagged windows need no model call and native masses for LR, PCA and AE are closed form.

findings.issue: The resource plan is unmeasured and incomplete against EXPERIMENT_DURABILITY_AND_RECOVERY.md Section 10 (mandatory for plans dated on or after 2026-09-05). Full-grid features are about 2.9 million windows x 232 features (2.7 GB float32, 5.5 GB float64) against about 1.1 GB available RAM, with no dtype, memmap or chunked-scoring rule, and PT1's byte-identity requires deterministic chunking. Episode occlusion cost is unbounded (n_episodes x 58 channels x 8 draws scored rows per replicate); at a drift-era flag rate of 20 percent isolation-forest scoring alone exceeds the 90-minute unit timeout. Missing owner fields: eta_basis_and_margin (no measured unit time), opaque_runtime_bound_admission, code_snapshot_path_and_sha256, local_delivery_and_verification_rule, progress stall threshold, terminal_status_paths, resume_validation_rule detail, aggregate/plot entrypoints, max_workers; the heartbeat lacks run_id, attempt_id, pid, completed/planned units and last checkpoint time.

findings.issue: delta = 0.06 is the largest synthetic native advantage over feature mass on the rank-equivalent AUROC scale, rounded up (recomputed: HGB 0.0545, PCA 0.019, AE 0.013, LR 0.008). The derivation is transparent and prespecified, but it means a SUPPORTED verdict is compatible with native explanations beating feature mass by as much as the synthetic worst case. The manuscript boundary does not require the claim wording to carry the margin.

findings.issue: z = (f - mean)/(sd + 1e-9) inherited from the synthetic core assumes no nominal feature column is constant. Real telemetry can hold a channel constant for the whole fit period or make a feature degenerate, giving z of order 1e9 that dominates PCA and AE reconstruction error, every reconstruction-based native mass and the feature-deviation mass. PT3 checks only finiteness, which such a column passes.

findings.required_change: Extend PT3 with 'every raw feature column has nominal-fit standard deviation > 1e-8 x max(1, |mean|)'. Prespecify handling for a failing column: freeze its standardized value at 0, record the column and channel in the run manifest, and flag masses of that channel in the per-event and per-episode tables.

Events of one class are near-replicates (21 class_7 anomalies on channels 14, 21 and 29), so the event bootstrap overstates the effective sample.

summary: The v2 candidate is faithful to the synthetic core, declares its deviations, keeps test labels out of every pre-evaluation stage, and its property tests can catch a plumbing leak. It cannot be frozen as written for five reasons: the non-inferiority rule has no assay-sensitivity gate and can return SUPPORTED at chance, since long events make detection near-automatic; the freeze may follow test-period scoring, so flag rates could be seen before rules lock; zero-order-hold staleness during unlabeled gaps can manufacture the false-alarm concentration Q-E2 measures; the lightweight E1 is empty (62 of 65 events affect all six channels); and the documented 2012-2013 drift needs a prespecified period split. Eleven further P2/P3 items are wording, fidelity or feasibility fixes.
